review.tagline: CLI that stores specs, tasks and session memory in your repo for coding agents
review.summary: Trellis is an npm CLI that writes a `.trellis/` directory into your repo holding specs, task PRDs and per-developer journals, then injects the relevant context into coding agent sessions. It runs a four-phase loop (plan, implement, verify, finish) using skills and sub-agents, and generates platform-specific files for 22 AI coding platforms.
review.audience: Teams using AI coding agents who want shared, persistent project standards
strengths: Specs, tasks and journals are plain files in the repo, reviewable like code
Same .trellis structure generated for 22 coding platforms, not just Claude Code
Verify step runs lint, type-check and tests against specs and self-fixes
Per-developer journals stay separate while shared specs live in git
weaknesses: AGPL-3.0 license may be a problem for some company use
Needs upfront effort to write or draft specs to get value
No tagged release listed; versions only via npm
